newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania economy on the mend says UNCTAD.
newsitem.headline: Romania economy on the mend says UNCTAD.

text.p: UNCTAD Secretary-General Rubens Ricupero on Wednesday painted an optimistic picture of Romania's success in bringing its economy towards European standards and its chances of receiving more foreign investment.

"Romania has made impressive progress in bringing down inflation...you are restructuring the economy...you are bringing in conditions for your integration into the European Union," Ricupero said on Wednesday.
He was speaking at a ceremony at Romania's Trade Ministry to launch two United Nations Conference on Trade and Development projects in the Balkan country.
The projects involve foreign trade personnel training and the opening of trade points to meet the needs of exporters and give them access to global information.
Romania, a UNCTAD member since 1964, has received UNCTAD technical assistance in other areas including customs, management of public debt and personnel training.
Romania, along with other ex-communist East European countries, is seeking full EU and NATO membership. It has an association accord with the EU since 1993.
"Economic growth has resumed and Romania will attract much foreign investment through privatisation," Ricupero said.
Romania, the second largest market in Eastern Europe after Poland, saw economic recovery from 1994, when its gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 3.9 percent.
The GDP increased 6.9 percent last year and is expected to post 4.8 percent growth in 1996.
In 1994, Romania also managed to slash 12-month inflation to 61.7 percent from around 300. Year-on-year inflation was 27.8 percent in 1995 and is forecast at 30 percent this year.

Last year Romania embarked on an ambitious mass sell-off offering up to 60 percent of around 4,000 state companies to adult Romanians in exchange for coupons and the rest for cash to local and foreign investors.
"Until now, foreign investment per year has been below the capacity of the country, but it will increase," Ricupero said.

Foreign investment into Romania since the end of communist rule in 1989 has been around $2.0 billion lei. Local analysts say the country needs much more and believe the economy is once more on a downward slide.
